project_title: The Gut Microbiome in Patients With Chronic Pancreatitis Is Characterized by Significant Dysbiosis and Overgrowth by Opportunistic Pathogens
project_description: 51 chronic pancreatitis patients vs 102 non-pancreatic-disease controls matched for age, sex, BMI, smoking, diabetes and stool elastase; fecal samples profiled by 16S rRNA gene sequencing (V1-V2 region).
citation: Frost et al. 2020, Clin Transl Gastroenterol, PMID 33094959
notes: Etiology: 68.6% alcohol-related (19.6% actively drinking), 25.5% idiopathic, 5.9% SPINK1-associated; 45.1% of patients on pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy, 54.9% on PPI. Controls were matched for exocrine pancreatic function (stool elastase), so findings are not explained by exocrine insufficiency alone. p from Mann-Whitney U; q is Benjamini-Hochberg FDR-adjusted (both reported, so findings are FDR-corrected, not merely nominal). Direction from sign of log(CP mean/control mean) in Table 2. Largest absolute increase in CP (mean 27.3% vs 16.7% in controls); log ratio +0.49.

project_title: Disordered Gut Microbiota in Children Who Have Chronic Pancreatitis and Different Functional Gene Mutations
project_description: 30 children with chronic pancreatitis vs 35 healthy controls; fecal samples profiled by 16S rRNA gene sequencing (V3-V4 region).
citation: Wang et al. 2020, Clin Transl Gastroenterol, PMID 32352720
notes: Pediatric chronic pancreatitis cohort, largely genetic (CFTR, CASR, CTSB, SPINK1, PRSS1 functional gene mutations); alcohol etiology not applicable. Exocrine insufficiency status and enzyme replacement therapy not reported. Listed by the authors as one of six genera with the greatest significant reductions in CCP relative to healthy controls (combined ROC AUC 0.92 for the six-genus panel). No per-genus p, q or LDA value is stated in the paper, so those columns are left blank rather than estimated. Multiple-testing correction not specified for this comparison.
